correctness.rationale: For all m>=1 on complex ell^2, the exact rational commutator entries form a strict-lower triangular row kernel a_n=1/[n(n+1)]. Dyadic diagonal blocks have s_k comparable to 1/(2^j k), since the strict ones matrix reduces to a finite integration matrix with explicit sine singular values. A two-regime dyadic counting sum yields N(t) comparable to t^{-1/2}, hence s_m(B) comparable to m^{-2}. All crossband rows form one rank-one operator per block with norm O(2^{-j}), so their remainder has exponentially decaying singular values. Ky Fan inequalities in both directions preserve the exact m^{-2} order. Endpoint p=1/2 follows from the harmonic-series divergence. Exact finite rational identities and trigonometric checks were replayed from the actual accompanying checker; computations are corroborative, not proofs of infinite bounds. No unproved lemma or boundary case is used.

The older Hardy operator approximation theorem works for non-atomic continuous integrals; its asymptotic regime is not the finite-dimensional dyadic-block lattice spectrum proved here. originality.rationale: Closest primary 2025 work introduces exactly the A_c row-difference family, but Theorems 1.3/5.8 establish its general Schatten criteria only for exponents above 1, while Theorem 5.5 gives a necessary inequality at p<=1 and the conclusion explicitly states the general classification remains missing. The new finding is the quantitative s_m~m^-2 rate for the natural specialization c_n=1/(n+1), producing a sharp weak endpoint not implied by those theorems. The 2026 discrete Mellin/Toeplitz manuscript concerns different sampled-kernel product defects, not the shift commutator singular numbers. Published published-finding corpus semantic queries found no equivalent claim. Abstract weighted Hardy results, unindexed publications, and incomplete manuscript coverage create acknowledged risks; originality is self-reviewed rather than independently certified.

value.rationale: This is a canonical, parameter-free commutator between the discrete Cesàro averaging operator and the unilateral shift generating the Toeplitz algebra. It quantifies how much they fail to commute by giving every singular value up to universal factors; the unexpectedly sharp quasi-Schatten cutoff p=1/2 is not a routine trace-class observation and is invisible to existing >1 Schatten classifications. Dyadic lattice saturation is a motivated mechanism that can inform endpoint analysis of difference-generated terraced matrices. The result is not an arbitrary finite slice, renaming, or tiny numerical gain.
